articles.title: Entenda a teoria que levou os vencedores do Nobel de Economia a mudar a política monetária | G1
articles.standfirst: Modelos desenvolvidos pelos economistas ajudam a explicar como as expectativas de consumidores e empresas influenciam decisões de juros, inflação e crescimento econômico.
articles.summary: Modelos desenvolvidos pelos economistas ajudam a explicar como as expectativas de consumidores e empresas influenciam decisões de juros, inflação e crescimento econômico.
articles.body:
O Prêmio Nobel de Economia deste ano foi concedido aos americanos Robert Hall e Michael Woodford. Os dois desenvolveram modelos que ajudam governos e bancos centrais a combater a recessão e a inflação.

Assim como no trânsito é preciso atenção para decidir quando frear ou acelerar, a condução da economia também depende de decisões tomadas no momento certo.

Nesse processo, os bancos centrais têm o papel de ajudar a controlar o ritmo da atividade econômica.

Quando a economia está aquecida demais, com inflação elevada e preços em alta, a tendência é aumentar os juros para conter o consumo. Já quando o crescimento perde força, a redução dos juros pode estimular a atividade econômica.

Os americanos Robert Hall e Michael Woodford venceram o Prêmio Nobel de Economia. — Foto: Globo/ Reprodução

Mas, para que essas decisões sejam eficazes, não basta analisar apenas os dados do passado.

Os vencedores do Nobel mostraram que, além de observar indicadores já conhecidos, é necessário prestar atenção às expectativas sobre o futuro.

Robert Hall e Michael Woodford criaram um modelo que forneceu base teórica para calibrar essas decisões e evitar, por exemplo, que um aumento excessivo dos juros provoque uma recessão.

O economista e professor da FGV, Aloisio Araujo, trabalhou com o Woodford. Ele disse que o colega mudou o jeito de os Bancos Centrais do mundo todo pilotarem a economia.

"O Banco Central tem uma participação muito importante na condução da política monetária e de moderar as oscilações econômicas. Não é neutro, está certo. A política dele tem efeitos na atividade econômica".

Para calcular esses efeitos, o Banco Central observa, hoje, os hábitos de consumidores e empresas, os dados de inflação e o crescimento econômico, mas mantém o olhar voltado para o futuro, levando em conta as expectativas de todos os agentes econômicos.

O Boletim Focus, divulgado semanalmente pelo Banco Central, reúne projeções de instituições financeiras para inflação, taxa de juros, crescimento do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) e câmbio. O levantamento funciona como uma forma de medir as expectativas do mercado para os próximos meses.

Essas expectativas influenciam diretamente as decisões de consumidores e empresas. A percepção sobre o futuro pode levar famílias a consumir mais ou menos, enquanto empresas podem decidir investir ou adiar projetos.

É justamente o equilíbrio entre oferta e demanda, entre o que é produzido e o que é consumido, que ajuda a determinar os preços no futuro.

Para os dois vencedores do Nobel, a estabilidade econômica depende da capacidade de governos e bancos centrais anteciparem movimentos, compreendendo e orientando as expectativas da sociedade.

A ideia é que, assim como no trânsito, a economia resulte da soma de milhões de decisões individuais que determinam o ritmo do fluxo.

articles.title: Meta's Muse AI agent brings back 73% of new users — nearly double ChatGPT's rate
articles.summary: New analysis from Sensor Tower shows Meta's Muse AI topping ChatGPT in new users — up to a point.
articles.body:
With Meta's ( META ) new Muse AI agent being the main driver of the stock price at the moment, digesting fresh data on its usage is fast becoming mission-critical for investors.

Here are some new numbers to feed the Muse beast, so to speak. All in all, they continue to paint Muse in a positive light.

Muse brings back 73% of new users the day after they install it, according to new analysis from Sensor Tower (see chart below). This is almost twice the rate of OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) ChatGPT. But Muse loses users quickly, and ChatGPT jumps ahead between days eight and nine.

Even so, Muse retains a solid number of users — enough to keep it in second place behind ChatGPT.

Daily active users for Muse keep climbing , hitting 2.182 million on Oct. 5, according to the latest data from Similarweb. Usage has risen steadily throughout October.

The increase may help soothe some concerns as Muse has reportedly hit a new hurdle: websites — Amazon ( AMZN ) being the top-of-mind example — blocking AI agents from browsing or completing purchases.

If Muse's usefulness becomes limited as more websites treat AI agents as bots or security risks, that could dent the new bullish case for the stock that has developed since the agent's September launch.

Deutsche Bank analyst Benjamin Black sees Muse reaching up to 8% of Meta's revenue by 2030, which nets out to roughly $36 billion in sales for the product. On the lower end of the prediction scale, Black sees Muse pulling in sales of $2.4 billion by 2030.

"In our view, Meta found a clear gap amongst current AI-agentic offerings — at the intersection of mobile app-based ecosystem, with a consumer-oriented UI which is seamless to use, the ability to complete transactions autonomously, free-to-use for the most part, and always-on feature within its own virtual machine — that makes it the service virtually unique in today's market," Black said.

This price reflects trading activity during the overnight session on the Blue Ocean ATS, available 8 PM to 4 AM ET, Sunday through Thursday, when regular markets are closed.

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show and the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team. Follow Sozzi on X @BrianSozzi , Instagram , and LinkedIn . Tips on stories? Email brian.sozzi@yahoofinance.com.

articles.title: Koch, Getty Families Team Up to Take Getty Images Private in Bankruptcy Deal
articles.summary: Getty Images Holdings Inc. will get an equity injection from existing shareholders as part of a prepackaged bankruptcy to restructure and take private the ph...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Getty Images Holdings Inc. will get an equity injection from existing shareholders as part of a prepackaged bankruptcy to restructure and take private the photo archive and stock-image company.

Members of the Getty family and Koch Equity Development, the investment arm of Koch Industries, Inc. will provide up to $433 million of new equity as part of the agreement, the company said in its restructuring support agreement disclosed on Monday.

As part of that amount, KED committed about $143 million in debtor-in-possession financing to fund the bankruptcy process. About $100 million of debt held by KED and its affiliates will also be converted into equity.

Getty reported $2.1 billion of debt as of June 30, but it redeemed its $628.4 million of 10.5% senior secured notes after its planned planned merger with Shutterstock Inc. fell through in July. As part of the restructuring, the $270 million senior unsecured notes will be retired, while secured creditors have agreed to extend the maturities and lower the interest paid for its holdings through new notes, term loans and revolving credit facility.

The company had entered into a voluntary grace period after it decided not to make interest payments on its unsecured notes due in Sept. 1 despite having the cash to pay in order to negotiate the restructuring. Bloomberg previously reported the Getty family's interest in injecting equity as part of the negotiations.

The company was founded in 1995 by Mark Getty, an heir to the Getty Oil fortune, and South African businessman Jonathan Klein. Through a series of acquisitions and partnerships it came to control some of the most iconic photographic images of all time. The business has changed ownership several times, however, and has struggled under its high debt load and a shift of customers using AI-generated images instead of stock photos.

With assistance from Christopher Palmeri.

articles.title: Satya Nadella went from H-1B worker to Microsoft CEO. The Trump administration just shut that path for his employees
articles.summary: Vice President JD Vance accused Microsoft of replacing laid-off Americans with “foreign indentured servants” and suspended it from the PERM green card progra...
articles.body:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has written that his story wouldn't be possible anywhere but the U.S. On Thursday, the Trump administration moved to block his company from helping its own foreign-born employees follow the path he took.

Vice President JD Vance announced on Oct. 8 that the administration is suspending Microsoft from the Labor Department's Permanent Labor Certification Program, known as PERM—usually the first step when an employer sponsors a foreign worker for a green card. Adobe and six IT services firms—Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services , Wipro, HCL Technologies, and Capgemini —were also suspended .

Hours later, President Donald Trump presented Nadella with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, one of the country's highest honors for innovation.

The Labor Department said it won't accept new PERM applications from the eight companies, nor process those already in the pipeline .

The move doesn't touch H-1B visas, the temporary work permits overseen by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. PERM comes later: To use it, an employer must advertise a job and show that no qualified, available U.S. worker can fill it before sponsoring a foreign employee for permanent residency . Most applicants are already working in the U.S. on H-1Bs.

Microsoft is the program's biggest user. The Labor Department ruled on 3,161 of its applications in the fiscal year that ended in September 2025, more than for any other employer, according to a GeekWire analysis .

Asked how long the suspension would last, Vance said it would "last as long as it needs to," adding that the administration has "a number of tools to suspend it indefinitely."

Doug Rand, a former senior USCIS advisor in the Biden administration, called the move "incoherent," telling the Associated Press that a green card frees a worker from depending on an employer for immigration status.

"So if the H-1B visa is how the people get into the country, the PERM program is how they stay in the United States to begin with," Vance said at a White House news conference . "Now there has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused the system more than Microsoft.

"Microsoft laid off last year 6,000 American workers," he said. "At the same time, the company benefited from 6,300 H-1B visas and almost 3,000 green cards." He added: "In other words, if you do the math, for every worker that Microsoft laid off, they replaced that worker with one and a half foreign indentured servants."

articles.title: Small Business’ AI Divide: A Minority Have Reaped Big Benefits, But Many Feel Unprepared
articles.summary: In a new survey, some businesses say concerns over privacy and data security have limited AI use. But it’s seen as a time saver and more AI spending is plann...
articles.body:
There's an artificial intelligence divide among the American small business community. A new survey of 200 small business owners finds virtually all (99%) are using artificial intelligence to some limited degree, and a minority report heavy use and big benefits.

Yet technology and AI stand out as the areas that the highest share of business owners say they feel "unprepared" to deal with. For example, while only 29% said they felt unprepared to deal with e-commerce and 35% with staffing issues, 40% said they were unprepared to deal with AI adoption and 43% with some aspect of technology or operations. (Overall, a whopping 97% "feel unprepared in at least one key area of their business," according to the study , conducted by Wakefield Research for TD Bank.)

While 61% said their use of AI had risen "somewhat" over the past six months, only 17% said it was significantly higher. The biggest barriers small businesses say prevents them from wrapping both arms around artificial intelligence? Almost a third, 31%, said it was concerns related to data privacy or security. Nearly a quarter, 24%, cited a lack of employee training. Other rationales included the cost, lack of employer knowledge regarding AI systems, and uncertainty over how AI would add value to the business.

How has AI helped small business users? In the survey, 57% of respondents said that utilizing AI saved time, 55% said it had improved cash flow decisions, 52% said it had helped increase sales and revenue, 42% said it was helpful in reducing overhead, and 41% said it had helped in detecting fraud.

Among small businesses that have willingly embraced AI, 17% reported using the technology had allowed them to significantly increase head counts–an outcome that other small business AI boosters have previously touted . While there are growing concerns about economy-wide job loss, particularly in certain white-collar and entry level positions , that doesn't mean that specific small businesses which successfully harness AI can't grow their share of the revenue pie enough to hire more workers.

Indeed, there's evidence in the TD Bank study that businesses do see themselves–happily or not–in a race for AI adoption. Some 62% of the businesses said they expected to seek new financing in the coming months. Of those, the top reason for needing financing (23% named it), was new equipment or technology; the second most cited reason (at 20%) was the need to invest in AI. Only 8% said they'd be using the financing for a new location or market.

articles.title: Oil Holds Advance as Expanding Middle East War Threatens Supply
articles.summary: Oil held a gain as a widening conflict in the Middle East threatened to hamper a recovery in supply from the region, while there were also doubts over US Pre...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Oil held a gain as a widening conflict in the Middle East threatened to hamper a recovery in supply from the region, while there were also doubts over US President Donald Trump's claims of an "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine.

West Texas Intermediate traded near $93 a barrel after rising 2.1% in the previous session, while Brent settled near $107 on Monday. A barrage of drone and missile attacks by Iran-backed Houthi militants on Saudi Arabia's main airport has intensified pressure on Washington to step up its efforts in the conflict in Yemen.

Meanwhile, Ukraine will continue attacks against Russia as Moscow keeps targeting its energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. Trump said there had been were violations of his "energy ceasefire" but urged his Ukrainian counterpart and Russian President Vladimir Putin to come together and end the war.

Brent remains more than 70% higher this year as the US war on Iran roils energy markets. The attacks on Saudi Arabia came shortly after Riyadh-led forces in Yemen launched a campaign to retake Houthi-held territory, while strikes on tankers in the critical Strait of Hormuz have escalated — leading a growing number of vessels to turn away from a port in the United Arab Emirates that has been key in helping Persian Gulf oil exports recover to near prewar levels.

"Its been a dizzying few days of headlines," said Scott Shelton, an energy specialist at TP ICAP Group, pointing to issues including Trump's claims of an "energy ceasefire" as well as the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. "We are off to a messy start this week."

With assistance from Weilun Soon and Lorelei Smillie.

articles.title: Fábio Felix: deputado mais votado do DF promete resistência | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao g1, deputado afirmou que vai atuar a favor de direitos trabalhistas e da população LGBTQIA+, além de articular contra medidas que considera 'retrocessos'.
articles.summary: Fábio Felix, deputado federal mais votado do DF, afirma que atuará em defesa dos direitos LGBTQIA+ e trabalhistas contra retrocessos no Congresso Nacional.
articles.body:
Assistente social, professor e primeiro deputado assumidamente gay da Câmara Legislativa ( CLDF ), Fábio Felix (PSOL) foi o deputado federal mais votado do Distrito Federal nas eleições de 2026 , com 224.224 votos.

O número foi quatro vezes maior que o número de votos que Felix recebeu em 2022, quando foi reeleito para a CLDF com 51.792 votos . Naquele ano, ele se tornou o distrital mais votado da história da capital.

Ao g1 , ele contou como foi a sua campanha e quais são as perspectivas para os próximos quatro anos de mandato na Câmara dos Deputados (veja vídeo acima).

O deputado eleito afirmou que pretende atuar a favor de direitos trabalhistas e da população LGBTQIA+ no Congresso Nacional . Segundo ele, o avanço de parlamentares conservadores exigirá articulação e resistência a medidas que considera retrocessos.

“Não há negociação para flexibilização de direitos. Nesse caso, não há qualquer negociação”, afirmou.

Apesar de prever um Congresso mais voltado ao enfrentamento político, Felix disse que estará aberto ao diálogo em pautas em que houver espaço para mediação.

Felix também afirmou que pretende trabalhar pela instalação de uma Comissão Parlamentar Mista de Inquérito (CPMI) para investigar o caso do Banco Master. Para ele, a investigação é importante diante dos impactos sobre o Banco de Brasília (BRB).

O deputado também destacou o custo de vida como uma das pautas que pretende levar para o debate nacional. Entre as propostas que citou estão a criação de uma legislação federal para controlar aumentos abusivos nos aluguéis e a tarifa zero no transporte público.

Ao avaliar a própria campanha, o deputado atribuiu parte do resultado à combinação entre mobilização nas ruas, atuação nas redes sociais e apresentação de propostas voltadas ao futuro.

Os votos em Felix representam quase o dobro do número conquistado pelo segundo deputado federal mais votado no DF, Rafael Prudente (PL), que recebeu 119.427 votos. Alberto Fraga (PL) foi o terceiro mais votado, com 118.579 .

🔎 Os deputados federais eleitos em 2026 tomam posse em 1º de fevereiro de 2027, para mandatos de quatro anos.

Quais pautas o senhor tá disposto a negociar e quais não aceita fazer concessões?

"Primeiro, não há cenário ruim que não haja resistência, né? Nós temos um Congresso mais conservador, o PL ganha força nas urnas e chega com muitos deputados federais na Câmara dos Deputados, mas a gente também tem uma alta renovação. Novos deputados e deputadas que chegam também com muito gás para fazer a diferença na Câmara dos Deputados do nosso campo, do campo progressista. Então, também estamos felizes em fazer o nosso trabalho e vamos ajudar a organizar a resistência no Distrito Federal e no Brasil inteiro.

Agora, existem pautas que a gente não negocia. O PL já disse no programa de governo do candidato deles que querem flexibilizar as leis trabalhistas, querem atacar direitos previdenciários, direitos dos servidores públicos com uma reforma da previdência, por exemplo. Eles lá atrás já tentaram flexibilizar os direitos da comunidade LGBT, tentaram revogar o casamento igualitário. Foi no governo Bolsonaro, por exemplo, que eles entraram, através da AGU, no Supremo contra a criminalização da homotransfobia. Então, não há negociação para flexibilização de direitos. Nesse caso, não há qualquer negociação.

Agora, pautas mais abrangentes, que houver espaço para mediação de algo, nós vamos estar sempre dispostos ao diálogo. Mas a gente sabe que vai ser um congresso muito mais voltado para o enfrentamento e a gente vai enfrentar para não deixar que os retrocessos aconteçam."

O senhor defende uma responsabilização, nesse caso, Master, e uma CPI na Câmara. Como o senhor pretende levar esse debate adiante e transformar essa responsabilização em algo para além do discurso político?

"Olha, eu acho que no Congresso Nacional a gente pode continuar a defesa de uma CPMI. A CPMI do Congresso chegou próximo às assinaturas necessárias para ser instalada e não foi instalada. Então, eu quero lutar, a partir de 2027, para que a gente tenha uma CPMI do Master, porque o Master tem tentáculos em várias instituições. Então, essa CPMI pode cumprir um papel muito importante de investigação e apuração desse caso.

E a gente sabe que o Distrito Federal, especialmente nosso banco público, o BRB, foi a principal vítima nacional do Vorcaro. Foi aqui que ele deixou um rombo de mais de R$ 12 bilhões e quem vai pagar essa conta? A gente não quer que seja a população do DF, a gente quer resgatar esse dinheiro, por isso eu vou para o Congresso Nacional lutar para que a gente tenha uma CPMI do Banco Master, para que esse caso seja investigado e para que a gente tenha condições de lutar para devolver o dinheiro para os bancos públicos do DF."

Como o senhor planeja o seu mandato e se prepara para os próximos quatro anos que estão por vir?

"É diferente quando você chega para um mandato parlamentar com uma força do voto popular tão expressivo como esse, eh, já já aconteceu isso comigo em 2022, né? Quando eu fui mais votado para deputado distrital, isso dá respaldo, dá possibilidade para você trabalhar, se engajar em pautas, defender causas. Então, isso é muito importante. E aí tem dois temas que eu me preocupo muito e que a gente vai precisar atuar no Congresso Nacional em 2027. O primeiro é a defesa do serviço dos servidores públicos e do serviço público.

Porque eles já vêm anunciando que querem fazer uma reforma administrativa, né? Querem atacar a estabilidade dos servidores, querem atacar direitos previdenciários. Então, eu quero estar muito engajado na frente parlamentar em defesa dos servidores públicos, porque eu acho que isso é muito importante para a nossa sociedade hoje. Os serviços públicos são fundamentais, porque eles alcançam a população que mais precisa. Só serve a esses que odeiam as políticas sociais atacar os serviços públicos e os servidores públicos. Então, vou me engajar muito nessa pauta.

E a segunda é, eu sou casado, né? E é um direito conquistado a partir de uma decisão do Supremo, entre outros direitos da comunidade LGBT. Então, a gente precisa reativar com muita força a frente parlamentar do Congresso Nacional em defesa dos direitos da população LGBT+ brasileira.

Eu quero estar engajado também nessa causa, porque nós não podemos tolerar retrocessos e agora nós temos uma bancada com mais de 10 deputados que são comprometidos com a causa e são pessoas LGBTs que vão estar com a gente nessa luta no Congresso Nacional. E diga-se de passagem, a maior bancada num Congresso Nacional de um país da América Latina."

O que acha que deu certo na sua campanha e pretende repetir, tanto no mandato, quanto no apoio às campanhas que vão para o segundo turno?

"A nossa campanha foi uma campanha muito militante, então, ela tinha duas características, era um pé na rua, um pé muito forte nas redes e defendendo propostas para mudar o futuro da população. Tem um tema que nós trouxemos aqui que teve muito respaldo, as pessoas se engajaram muito, que é estabelecer uma legislação federal para controle do aumento abusivo dos aluguéis. Os aluguéis, a questão da moradia, hoje, é uma questão central, as pessoas estão gastando muito dinheiro com isso.

Então, esse é um aporte que eu já levei para a campanha, né, do presidente Lula, nós já levamos em algumas reuniões para esse segundo turno. É preciso discutir o custo de vida, tarifa zero no transporte público e o controle do aumento abusivo dos aluguéis. Eu acho que são temas importantes, sempre com o pé na rua e não é só estar na rua bandeirando, agitando, visual, é estar na rua conversando com as pessoas, convencendo. Esse foi o perfil da nossa campanha. E uma campanha que se comunica a partir dessas pautas de futuro, dando uma perspectiva para as pessoas, se comunica diretamente com as pessoas via as redes sociais, né?

A gente conversando diretamente, olhando para a câmera, dialogando com as pessoas, eh, interagindo nos comentários e ouvindo o que que a população tem a dizer que tá ali nas redes. As pessoas, hoje, de 24 horas do dia, passam 9 horas em média nas telas. Então, querendo ou não, nós precisamos estabelecer esse diálogo direto e a nossa campanha também, eh, buscou estabelecer esse diálogo, que eu acho que isso também se conecta mais com as pessoas, mas sempre nos pautando, né, por mudanças e projetos de futuro para a maioria da nossa população."

Fábio Felix, em sessão na Câmara Legislativa do DF — Foto: Sara Marques/Agência CLDF

Na Câmara do DF, Fábio Felix presidiu, a partir de 2019, a Comissão de Direitos Humanos. Foram mais de 8 mil denúncias recebidas enquanto ele esteve à frente do grupo.

Ele também atuou nas comissões Parlamentares de Inquérito (CPI) do Feminicídio e dos Atos Antidemocráticos, que tratou dos ataques aos Três Poderes, em 8 de janeiro de 2023, além de ter feito parte da Comissão Especial da Vacina, durante a pandemia da Covid-19.

O deputado federal Fábio Felix, com leque com as cores da bandeira LGBT e o Congresso Nacional ao fundo — Foto: Reprodução/Fábio Felix

Formado na Universidade de Brasília (UnB), atuou como assistente social na Rodoviária do Plano Piloto, com adolescentes em situação de rua, e depois no antigo CAJE, o centro de internação de menores do DF, onde denunciou tortura e violação de direitos de adolescentes em cumprimento de medida socioeducativa.

Também presidiu o Conselho Distrital dos Direitos da Criança e do Adolescente. É professor e servidor do sistema socioeducativo. Fábio Felix também é ativista da causa LGBTQIA+.

Em 2018, foi eleito o primeiro deputado distrital assumidamente gay da Câmara Legislativa do DF. Em 2022, foi reeleito com 51.792 votos, tornando-se o parlamentar mais votado na história de Brasília.

articles.title: Trump’s Diesel Deal Irks Allies and Is Unlikely to Reduce Prices
articles.summary: President Donald Trump’s deal for Russian diesel exposed the US to legal questions, opened a rift with his Republican allies and European leaders and heighte...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- President Donald Trump's deal for Russian diesel exposed the US to legal questions, opened a rift with his Republican allies and European leaders and heightened tensions with Ukraine — all in exchange for an outcome that experts suggest is unlikely to succeed.

Under the agreement — announced late last week — Russian President Vladimir Putin would begin releasing diesel supplies into global markets as part of a US effort to bring down prices from their record highs before the Nov. 3 midterm elections. Trump has also intensified demands on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop attacking Russian refineries and announced an energy ceasefire between the two sides.

The decisions and the ceasefire are all a bet that lowering fuel prices will be the best way to win more votes next month despite the risk of a backlash from political friends and foes alike. On Sunday, a bipartisan group of senators argued that Trump should "reverse course" on his plan to cut a diesel deal with Russia.

"The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians," the senators said in a statement.

The accord also provoked fresh tension with Europe, where officials warned that it would bolster Moscow's war effort in Ukraine. They said the US should impose more sanctions instead.

"We would call on the US to put the sanctions in place so that actually we could finish this war, so that all the effects of these attacks on refineries would not be there," top European Union diplomat Kaja Kallas told reporters in Luxembourg on Monday before meeting with the bloc's foreign ministers.

There's also the legal challenge. A 2022 law prohibits the US from buying most Russian energy products. It's still not clear how Trump plans to get around that, and some lawmakers, including Senator Roger Wicker, a Mississippi Republican, have already said they don't expect the deal to go through.

Trump acknowledged on Monday that neither side had actually committed to stop attacking each other's energy infrastructure.

"They agreed. You know why? Because I said you agree," Trump told reporters. "That's why they agreed — because I said they agreed."

articles.title: Oil prices hold near $105 per barrel as Trump eases sanctions on Russian fuel
articles.summary: Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday after rising by nearly $2 a barrel in the previous session, as traders weighed the risks to supplies from attacks on
articles.body: Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday after rising by nearly $2 a barrel in the previous session, as traders weighed the risks to supplies from attacks on Saudi Arabia against the prospect of additional diesel supplies from Russia.West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude was trading at $92.84 a barrel, down $0.90, or 0.96%, while Brent crude fell $1.01, or 0.95%, to $105.60 a barrel. This comes after Brent futures had settled at $106.65 a barrel on Monday, their highest level since September 15.Oil markets have found some relief after US President Donald Trump said that Russia has agreed to supply diesel to global markets. The US administation temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel, which were designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its war on Ukraine.These additional supplies could ease tightness in global fuel markets and temper some of the supply concerns that have supported crude prices in recent weeks.However, lawmakers from both parties in the US complained that Trump's agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin appeared to violate US law barring imports of Russian energy until Moscow ends its aggression against Ukraine.Concerns about the vulnerability of energy infrastructure and shipping lanes in the Gulf continued to weigh on market sentiment after Iran-aligned Houthis struck Riyadh's international airport over the weekend. Attacks on tankers were also reported near the Strait of Hormuz.The incidents threatened to derail the recovery in Middle East supplies seen in September, reinforcing concerns about further disruptions along one of the world's most important energy transit routes.Ministers of OPEC and non-OPEC Participating Countries in the Declaration of Cooperation said shipping and insurance costs had surged to unprecedented levels, exceeding one-third of the commodity value. The higher costs were impeding the efficient movement of crude oil and petroleum products.OPEC has also lowered its forecast for oil demand growth this year to 400,000 barrels per day (bpd), from 1.4 million bpd at the start of the year, reflecting developments throughout the year, the organisation's secretary general, Haitham Al Ghais, said on Monday, as cited by Reuters.Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs said that brent crude prices could fall to the $60s per barrel in 2027 if oil production in the Persian Gulf recovers faster than expected. However, the investment bank warned that further escalation in the region could push prices significantly higher.The bank said Brent could decline to the $60s if average oil output in the Gulf in 2027 rises by 1 million bpd above February 2026 levels.“A faster recovery in Mideast output and/or a faster erosion of the risk premium are the most likely potential triggers of price downside,” Goldman Sachs said.Continued adjustments in Middle East oil supplies would eventually bring crude prices down but renewed escalation in the region remained a significant risk that could push prices higher.Now, the Middle East conflict has continued disrupt energy supplies for over seven months now, rattling oil markets and pushing prices high. However, even with the ongoing tensions, the spike is far lower than the $126 per barrel seen earlier during the crisis.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Treasuries Gain on Haven Demand as Trading Resumes After Holiday
articles.summary: Treasuries advanced as trading resumed after a long weekend, with a slide in Asian equities fueling demand for haven assets.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Treasuries advanced as trading resumed after a long weekend, with a slide in Asian equities fueling demand for haven assets.

The 10-year US yield slid as much as 5 basis points to about 5.19% on Tuesday, as Asia's stock benchmark slumped about 2%. There was no cash trading in Treasuries globally on Monday due to holidays in the US and Japan.

"Risk-off on equities," Michael Tang, a rates strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia in Sydney, said when asked about the rally in US bonds.

articles.title: India's economic story in fast lane, IMF projects 7% GDP growth for FY26 and FY27
articles.summary: India’s economy is expected to grow by 7% in both 2026 and 2027, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), keeping the country among the
articles.body: India’s economy is expected to grow by 7% in both 2026 and 2027, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), keeping the country among the fastest-growing major economies despite growing uncertainties. This reflects stronger-than-expected momentum, supported by resilient domestic demand and robust services activity.”It also highlighted how the Indian economy continued to expand despite rising oil prices. “India’s growth remained robust, underpinned by domestic demand and services, despite higher oil prices.”The improved outlook follows the stronger-than-expected GDP growth recorded in the April-June quarter, prompting several global institutions, including the World Bank, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), S&P Global Ratings, Moody's Ratings, Fitch Ratings and the Asian Development Bank (ADB), to raise their growth estimates for India.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();World Bank, OECD raise India growth forecastsThe World Bank raised its growth projection for India in 2026-27 to 7.1%, from 6.6% estimated earlier. The multilateral agency attributed the revision to strong domestic demand and exports, despite global headwinds. It expects the economy to grow by 7.2% in 2027-28.The OECD has also increased its forecast for India's GDP growth in 2026-27 to 7.1%, from 6.3% projected in June. The revised estimate is higher than the 7% forecasts from S&P, Moody's and ADB, while Fitch expects growth of 6.9%.Moody's Ratings raised its forecast for India's real GDP growth in FY27 to 7%, from 6%, citing the economy's resilience amid the Middle East conflict."Although we continue to expect India to grow faster than all other G-20 economies, as well as similarly rated emerging market sovereigns, risks remain," Moody’s said.Expansion in the April-June quarter was supported by strong investment and manufacturing activity, which helped offset weakness in mining and consumer-facing services.Global growth faces a more fragile outlookWhile India has received a series of growth upgrades, the IMF has warned that the global economy's resilience is becoming increasingly fragile and uneven.“The global economy remains resilient, but that resilience is becoming more fragile and more uneven. articles.title: Chip selloff extends as South Korean stock market sinks 6%
articles.summary: Micron and SK Hynix shares dropped in a sell-off of the KOSPI as Chinese chip makers ramp up competition.
articles.body:
Shares of Micron ( MU ) and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) are poised to open lower on Tuesday, extending a global sell-off in memory-chip stocks as South Korea's benchmark KOSPI ( ^KS11 I) tanked 6%.

In South Korea, SK Hynix ( 000660.KS ) and Samsung Electronics ( 005930.KS ) each fell roughly 8%, extending their losing streaks to five sessions. The two chipmakers account for more than half of the South Korean stock market's total capitalization.

The sell-off was a continuation of market reaction after Chinese memory maker CXMT ( 688825.SS ) announced progress on a new memory-cell design engineered to pack more storage into less physical space.

CXMT aims to introduce a new server memory product built on this architecture by the end of 2026.

The advance threatens to intensify competition for Samsung, SK Hynix, and US-based Micron, which together account for roughly 90% of the global DRAM market.

This price reflects trading activity during the overnight session on the Blue Ocean ATS, available 8 PM to 4 AM ET, Sunday through Thursday, when regular markets are closed.

Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung have been major beneficiaries of the AI trade over the past year amid surging demand for memory and storage chips driven by the global AI data center build-out. All three memory makers reached $1 trillion valuation over the summer.

Last week, Samsung reported a preliminary record third quarter profit of $80 billion, but the forecast did little to lift the rest of the chip sector

Micron posted strong quarterly results in September . The stock is up roughly 240% year-to-date.

Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: Tenant claimed landlords withheld Rs 10 lakh security deposit and refused to vacate shop; Delhi High Court rules against him, orders payout for unauthorised stay
articles.summary: Whether as a tenant or as a landlord, a proper paper trail is important to avoid disputes in future, and even if they do arise to prove your claim.
articles.body: Whether as a tenant or as a landlord, a proper paper trail is important to avoid disputes in future, and even if they do arise to prove your claim. In a recent ruling, the court asked the tenant to vacate and also pay for what was ruled to be an unauthorised stay.On September 28, 2026, the Delhi High Court directed the tenant to vacate the premises and pay mesne profits to the landlords for the period during which he continued to occupy the shop without authorisation.What the case is about:The case involved a tenant, who rented a 238.38 sq. ft shop in 2014 from a couple in Delhi. The agreed monthly rent was Rs 25,500. However, the 11-month rent agreement was never registered.Also Read | Landlords wanted tenant out to open a law office; he said the reason for seeking eviction had changed and other properties were available, why Delhi High Court upheld evictionThe tenant subsequently claimed that he had paid the landlords Rs 10 lakh in cash as a security deposit between November 2016 and March 2017. However, he could not produce a receipt or any other documentary evidence to establish that the payment had been made.The tenant also told the court that rent agreements had been signed in 2015 at the same monthly rent and another agreement was executed in 2017. According to him, all these unregistered agreements had been prepared by the landlord couple.The dispute escalated in 2018, when another rent agreement was signed. The landlords maintained that the new agreement increased the monthly rent to Rs 29,000. Like the earlier agreements, this one was also unregistered and covered a period of 11 months.Although the tenant acknowledged that a fresh agreement had been executed in 2018, he disputed the claimed increase in rent. He argued that the monthly rent had actually been fixed at Rs 2,900, rather than Rs 29,000, because he had already paid a security deposit of Rs 10 lakh in the preceding years. The landlord couple firmly rejected his contention.When the 2018 rent agreement expired in 2019, the landlords asked the tenant to vacate the shop and hand over possession. The tenant, however, refused to leave unless his claimed security deposit of Rs 10 lakh was returned. The disagreement eventually developed into a legal dispute that reached the Delhi High Court.Also Read | Woman buys Rs 1.03 crore 3BHK in Bengaluru, but builder fails to provide specially-enabled parking; Karnataka RERA orders provision within 60 days and audited maintenance accountsWhy did the tenant lose the case?The Delhi High Court noted that the tenant’s defence was based on his claim that he had paid the landlords Rs 10 lakh as a security deposit between November 2016 and 2017 in exchange for the shop. He maintained that, following this arrangement, he regularly paid monthly rent of Rs 2,900. The landlady, however, disputed his version and insisted that the rent was Rs 29,000 per month, not Rs 2,900.During her deposition before the District Court, the landlady stated that the monthly rent under the first agreement in 2014 was Rs 25,500 and that it had increased to Rs 29,000 in 2018. She also said that these details were reflected in her income tax return (ITR), according to an ET report.Her statement before the Delhi High Court was different. She said the tenant wanted to avoid paying GST and income tax, which was why the rent was collected in cash without issuing receipts. She further admitted before the High Court that she had not reported this rental income to the tax authorities.The landlord couple produced the 2018 rent agreement before the court. The tenant initially disputed the document, alleging that his signature on it had been forged and that the agreement was fabricated. However, he later acknowledged before the Delhi High Court that the 2018 rent agreement had been executed. This admission was inconsistent with his earlier denial, the ET report said.Also Read | Retired bank employee got Rs 12.27 lakh leave encashment and claimed Rs 3 lakh exemption in 2020, but government later hiked limit to Rs 25 lakh in 2023; ITAT Chennai allows full tax exemptionWhen the tenant’s mother appeared before the court as a witness, she stated that the shop had been rented in 2014 at a monthly rent of Rs 25,500. She also denied having issued any receipt or paid Rs 4.5 lakh, which was supposedly part of the total Rs 10 lakh security deposit mentioned in her affidavit.Her testimony raised doubts about the tenant’s claim that he had paid the landlords Rs 10 lakh as a security deposit. In particular, the Delhi High Court took note of the fact that his own mother denied the payment of Rs 4.5 lakh referred to in her affidavit.The court further observed that the tenant had not shown that he attempted to record the alleged Rs 10 lakh arrangement in the rent agreements executed in 2016, 2017 and 2018. None of these agreements had been produced as evidence to substantiate his claim.As a result, the tenant failed to establish that he had paid the claimed Rs 10 lakh security deposit.Saumya Brajmohan, Partner at Solomon & Co, told ET that the tenant’s own statements weakened his defence, while he failed to produce evidence to support the key claims on which his case rested.In particular, he could not establish that he had paid Rs 10 lakh under a mortgage or security deposit arrangement, or that this payment had led to a reduction in the monthly rent to Rs 2,900.Another setback for the tenant was his failure to produce the rent agreements that he had acknowledged signing. He was also unable to demonstrate that any of these agreements documented the alleged Rs 10 lakh mortgage or security arrangement.Brajmohan says: "In other words, Mendiratta (tenant’s) fundamental problem was evidentiary: his pleadings, his cross-examination, and the evidence he led did not establish the alternative version of the tenancy that he relied upon.”The court found that his continued occupation of the shop after the tenancy ended up as being unauthorised and directed him to pay mesne profits for the period during which he remained in possession.Also Read | Sisters sought share in parents’ properties under Hindu Succession law; Madras HC rules for brother over mother’s land on ouster, father’s estate over missing partiesYou use AI every day. articles.title: Rupee extends winning streak, rises to 94.96 against dollar as RBI tightens forex rules
articles.summary: Rupee extended its winning streak on Tuesday, strengthening to 94.96 against the US dollar.
articles.body: Rupee extended its winning streak on Tuesday, strengthening to 94.96 against the US dollar. The currency opened at 95.53 in the interbank market and rose 82 paise or 0.7% from its previous close. The latest gains come after rupee's sharp rally on Monday, when it rose 93 paise to close at 95.78 against the dollar, clocking its biggest single-day gain in more than six months.The currency's recovery is attributed to a series of steps taken by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to ease immediate dollar demand and restrict excessive positions in the foreign exchange market. Forex traders expect these measures to reduce demand for dollars in the spot market and limit speculative bets against the rupee.Among the steps announced by the central bank are a dedicated dollar window for oil marketing companies through designated banks and higher costs for certain foreign exchange hedging transactions."With the RBI's measures supporting the rupee, we expect USD/INR to move towards 95.00–94.80 range in the near term," CR Forex Advisors MD Amit Pabari told PTI.RBI moves, Dalal Street and more in focusThe central bank announced tighter rules for foreign exchange derivatives on Saturday as part of its efforts to curb speculative positions against rupee. Banks have also been asked to set aside a 20% reserve for dollar purchases exceeding $2 million.Separately, the RBI directed authorised dealers (AD) not to allow users to rebook cancelled foreign exchange derivative contracts involving the rupee. The restriction applies to both deliverable and non-deliverable contracts.The dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of six currencies, slipped 0.15% to 102.43.Oil prices also moved lower, with Brent crude futures, the global oil benchmark, falling 1.11% to $105.47 per barrel.Alongside a stronger rupee, Dalal Street was also trading higher on Tuesday. BSE Sensex gained over 600 points to reach 72,584.50, while NSE Nifty advanced 200 points to 22,575.30.Foreign institutional investors, however, continued to sell equities. According to exchange data, FIIs were net sellers to the tune of Rs 1,708.48 crore on Monday.Separately, government data released on Monday showed that retail inflation rose sharply to 5.54% in September, largely on account of higher onion and other food prices. The increase, however, kept inflation within the RBI's tolerance band.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Power to empower': PM Modi stresses need to make tech progress accessible to all
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday called for technology, data, knowledge and innovation to be used to empower people and create
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday called for technology, data, knowledge and innovation to be used to empower people and create opportunities for millions, saying the real question was not who possessed power but how it was used.PM Modi said India’s approach should focus on enabling people, promoting collaboration and helping others succeed rather than concentrating on control or competition.“Today, technology is power, data is power, knowledge is power, and innovation is power. But, the real question is not who has the power, but how it is being used. Will technology advance only a few people or create new opportunities for millions? Will knowledge remain the strength of a select few or enhance everyone's capabilities? This is where a new idea is born: power to empower. Moving beyond power to control, we need power to enable. Moving beyond power to compete, we need power to collaborate. And moving beyond power to succeed, we need power to help others succeed,” the Prime Minister added. He made these remarks while addressing the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi.PM Modi said the principle of using knowledge, wealth and power for a larger purpose was rooted in India's traditions.“This is not new to India. We have always emphasised the importance of utilisation of knowledge, money, and power. The real value of power lies in its purpose,” he said.“Whoever possesses knowledge, wealth, and power, how they use it is crucial. The true value of power lies in its purpose, and it's crucial to understand this philosophy in today's times... Our thousands of years of tradition have taught us this, and in India, we have demonstrated its application in our governance and work culture,” he added.The Prime Minister also described India as the “mother of democracy” and said the country was focused on making technology more accessible to people across regions and economic backgrounds.“India focussed on making mobile data affordable, even students from small cities can have access to digital learning,” he said.PM Modi also underlined India's approach to global economic growth, saying, “We do not grow at anyone's cost, we grow with and for the world.”The Prime Minister said the government's role should be to strengthen citizens rather than make them dependent on the system.“The government has authority, but its purpose should not be to make its citizens dependent on the system. Rather, its purpose should be to strengthen and empower its citizens, and India is on this path. Following this path, India has lifted 250 million people out of poverty in the last ten years – more than the population of many countries in the world,” he said.Modi also cited the AI Impact Summit held in India, saying discussions had explored how artificial intelligence could benefit both people and animals.“AI Impact Summit was held in India, and Bloomberg also praised it highly. In this summit, alongside utilizing AI for humanity, how animals can benefit from AI was also made a topic of discussion... This demonstrates that the more capable India becomes, the more beneficial it is for humanity and the world,” he said.Welcoming the decision to host the forum in India for the first time, PM Modi said Bloomberg founder Michael Bloomberg had chosen the right place at the right time.“Every year at this forum, we discuss economy, energy, etc. For the first time, it’s been held in India. I’d like to say to Mr. Bloomberg that he has chosen the right place at the right time,” he said.The eighth edition of the Bloomberg New Economy Forum brought together more than 500 public- and private-sector leaders from around the world. Held under the theme “A World in Play: Defining the New Levers of Power,” the forum focused on shifting geopolitical dynamics, emerging risks and opportunities, and ways to support future economic growth.In a message ahead of the event, PM Modi said India was moving beyond being an investment destination to becoming a partner in shaping the global economy.“Today, India stands at a defining moment in its journey. India is no longer just a destination for investment; it is a trusted partner in shaping the global future. In our pursuit of Viksit Bharat (Developed India), we are working to build one of the most reliable growth engines of the world and a balanced world economic order,” he said.He added that the forum would give participants an opportunity to experience a country that was “not just participating in the new economy, but actively defining it.”You use AI every day. articles.title: Power generation up 11% y-o-y in Q2: CREA
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s electricity generation rose 11% year-on-year to 536 billion units (BU) in the second quarter of 2026-27, while peak power demand
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s electricity generation rose 11% year-on-year to 536 billion units (BU) in the second quarter of 2026-27, while peak power demand touched a record 270 GW, 18% higher than the peak recorded in the corresponding period last year.Despite the surge in demand, coal-fired power plants were not operating at full capacity, pointing to significant headroom in the existing fleet even as renewable generation continued to expand, according to a report by Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA).Renewable electricity generation, excluding large hydropower, crossed 100 BU for the first time in a quarter. Solar generation rose 39% year-on-year to 51 BU, while wind generation increased 29% to 45 BU. Solar accounted for 10% of total electricity generation for the first time, setting a daily record of 705 million units (MU) on Sept 30.Combined generation from non-fossil sources, including renewables, large hydropower and nuclear, reached a record 177 BU, up from 163 BU a year earlier. Thermal power continued to dominate the generation mix, accounting for 64% of total electricity generation.Coal-fired power plant utilisation fell to 68% in Q2 from 73% in the first quarter, while coal despatches to power plants declined from 74 million tonnes in May to 66 million tonnes in Aug, the lowest level recorded in 2026. CREA said the figures indicated that the coal fleet had substantial unused capacity even during periods of record electricity demand.Large hydropower generation rose to 60 BU from 39 BU in the first quarter, but remained 20% below the year-earlier level, as deficient rainfall amid El Niño conditions led to a shortfall.India’s installed power capacity stood at 555 GW in Aug, with non-fossil sources accounting for around 55% of capacity. CREA said the pipeline of battery and pumped-hydro storage projects had reached around 290 GWh, though only 9.1 GWh was operational.“As solar increasingly meets daytime electricity demand and storage helps meet evening and night-time peaks, new thermal capacity should be assessed against expected demand, renewable generation and storage availability. This will help avoid building capacity that could remain underutilised as India’s power system evolves,” said Manoj Kumar, India analyst at CREA.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.body: Gold price prediction today: Gold prices may rise in the short-term but the upside is likely to be capped, says Praveen Singh, Head Currencies and Commodities, Mirae Asset ShareKhan. Let’s take a look:Gold Performance:On October 12, spot gold surrendered its gains made in the Asian session to slide lower as the day wore on as oil prices and Dollar Index strengthened.At the time of writing this article on the night of October 12, spot gold was changing hands at $4165, down nearly 0.7% for the day. Losses in domestic gold prices were more pronounced, down 1.3%, due to strong appreciation in the INR on significant steps taken by the RBI to support the ailing currency in the weekend.In the week ending October 9, the shiny metal closed with a weekly gain of 1.2% at $4194, though return of Chinese buyers after a week-long ‘golden week holiday’ helped the metal cushion its losses.Geopolitics and oil:A weekend attack on Saudi's Riyadh Airport on Saturday left 12 people dead, including an American, and over 300 injured. Saudi Arabia said it was dealing with missiles and drone attacks Monday also. The US President Trump said he is weighing joining war against the Houthis.The conflict between the Houthis and Yemen’s internationally recognised government, backed by Saudi Arabia, has intensified regional geopolitical tensions. Houthi attacks on Riyadh and the resulting aviation disruptions have affected the ongoing World Petroleum Congress, prompting several senior oil executives to withdraw from in-person participation, although the event is proceeding as planned. Attention will subsequently shift to the Future Investment Initiative, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s flagship investment conference, scheduled for October 26-29. Given the prominence of these events and continued Houthi warnings concerning Saudi airspace, the risk of further attacks is likely to remain elevated.Trump’s announcement of an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine does not seem to be holding.Trump, through a social media post claimed that Russia has agreed to sell US diesel to the tune of 4.8 million tons in the coming months. Russia has not specified either dates or volumes. The initial tranche of 5,00,000 tons (125,000 bpd if spread across November) will be less than 10% of the diesel loss of 1.6 mbpd. The US consumes around 3.5-4 mb diesel/day. Even 4.8 million tons, promised to be delivered by the start of the next year, amount to merely 36 mb, well short of the US consumption.At the time of writing, Brent oil futures were trading with a daily gain of 2% at $106.75.Data roundup:Friday’s US data showed that University of Michigan sentiment fell from 48.1 in September to 46.30 (forecast 47.60), lowest since May, in its October preliminary reading. One-year inflation expectations rose from 4.6% to 4.7%, while five-ten-year expectations edged higher from 3.4% to 3.5%. Current conditions slumped sharply from 50.90 to 44.70 (forecast 50.10), a record low.NY Fed one-year consumers' inflation expectations rose to 3.90% in September — the highest since May 2023.The US trade deficit in August increased to its highest level since March 2025 as imports hit a record high of $420.80 billion.Currencies and yields:Indian Rupee strengthened Monday as the RBI took extraordinary measures on October 10 to support the ailing domestic currency. These steps include to open a special window to meet state-run oil companies’ requirements, asking banks to park cash with the RBI for some forex transactions (equivalent of 20% of the notional amount of each derivative transaction exceeding $2 million), prohibiting dealers from re-booking cancelled forex derivatives involving the INR, and reduction in limits for forex derivative transactions without confirmed existence of the underlying assets to $5 million from $100 million.The US Dollar Index edged higher Monday as crude oil prices rose. The Index, at the time of writing, was hovering around 102.51, up nearly 0.25% for the day, as it approached the cycle high of 102.53, highest since April 10, 2025. The US bond market was closed to observe the ‘Columbus Day’ holiday.Fed rate hike probability: October Fed rate hike probability continues to fluctuate around 20%; in the last three weeks, the probability has fallen sharply from 70% following a weak non-farm payroll report for September and dovish Fed commentary.Markets see the Fed hiking rates three times by June 2027, though.2026 LBMA’s annual conference:The two-day Global Precious Metals Conference underscored the fundamental case for gold on central banks diversifying their reserves; geopolitical polarization and fragmentation reshaping the global monetary system; and rising concerns over sovereign debt.Participants see gold prices trading around $5,013.30 an ounce by this time next year.CFTC positioning: Hedge fund managers cut their net bullish god bets to 15-week low as they reduced their net-long positions by 9598 lots to 114,820 in the week ending October 6, according to weekly CFTC data.Long-only positions fell 4,411 lots to 130,247 in the week ending Oct. 6. The long-only total was the lowest in 16 weeks, while short-only positions rose 5,187 lots to 15,427 -- the highest in 10 weeks.Gold ETF and COMEX inventory: Total known global ETF holdings slipped on October 9 to 101.12 Moz after rising for five days in a row. ETF investors sold 177,800 Ounces on October 9, most in 2 months. However, ETF holdings are up 2.17 Moz YTD after a huge turnaround in ETF flows since the cycle low of 96.16 MOz reached on July 20. Holdings are up ~0.20 Moz since the beginning of the Iran conflict on February 28.Registered COMEX inventory at 15.07 Moz, has remained nearly steady since September 30. It is down nearly 38% since the record peak of 24.25 MOz reached in April 2025. Fedspeak: Speaking on economic outlook and monetary policy at National Association for Business Economics on October 12, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, a Fed hawk, said business pricing power and a sturdy economy show that interest rates are not high enough to tame inflation. She added that frequent and smaller rate increases are preferred over big rate hikes to allow businesses to adjust.Upcoming data: Major US data on cards this week include weekly ADP employment change (October 13), September CPI inflation (October 14), September retail sales (October 15), Philadelphia Fed Business outlook (October 15) and September PPI inflation (October 15).Focus will be on Germany's and France's CPI data, too, which will be released on October 13 and October 15, respectively.UK's monthly GDP data will be released on October 15.Upcoming events: Investors will pay attention to speeches of a battery of Fed speakers lined up in near term. The list of the Fed speakers includes Collins, Hammack, Waller, Barkin, and Bowman.The Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will participate in a fireside chat with IMF MD Georgieva at IMF's annual gathering on October 16 in Bangkok, Thailand.Gold Price Outlook:Healthy ETF inflows and reduced Fed rate hike support the shiny metal; however, strong risk appetite, surging oil prices, elevated yields, and high probability of Fed rate hike in the coming months continue to pressurize the metal.Going ahead, focus will be mainly on Warsh’s talk and US CPI data.In the very short term, gold may push higher, but upside is likely to be contained unless some other major fundamental factor crops up in the picture/oil prices fall sharply. Oil could be a tug of war between the US and Iran as November 3midterm elections approach.Support is at 4150/4100/$4000, while resistance is seen at 4225/4255/4280/4337.Trading the range (buying the dips/selling into rallies) with a suitable and tight stop-loss is advisable presently. It is to be noted that domestic gold prices are expected to be under additional pressure due to the possibility of the domestic currency strengthening further on the RBI’s measures.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.title: Precio de la luz por horas hoy, martes 13 de octubre: cuándo es más barata y más cara
articles.standfirst: El precio de la luz sube notablemente este martes
articles.summary: El precio de la luz sube notablemente este martes
articles.body: El precio medio de la electricidad de hoy, 166,63 €/MWh, representa un aumento de 14,87 € respecto al día anterior, donde se registró un precio de 151,76 €/MWh. Este martes, los consumidores experimentan una notable subida en la factura eléctrica. A continuación, se analizarán las horas más caras y más baratas del día. El costo de la luz alcanza sus máximos entre las 20:00 y las 22:00, donde se registran los precios más altos del día. Durante este bloque, las tarifas superan los 260 €/MWh, alcanzando un pico de 260.62 €/MWh a las 20:00. Además, se observan precios elevados desde las 18:00 hasta las 21:00, lo que indica una tendencia de encarecimiento en las horas de mayor demanda energética. La luz es más barata durante los tramos nocturnos y en las primeras horas de la tarde, lo que brinda a los consumidores oportunidades significativas de ahorro. Entre las franjas horarias más relevantes, se destacan los tramos de 12:00 a 15:00 donde los precios son notablemente bajos, alcanzando 39.8 €/MWh a las 12:00 y 33.3 €/MWh a las 14:00, con el punto más bajo a las 15:00 con 26.25 €/MWh. Además, se observan precios competitivos entre la 01:00 y las 04:00, con valores que oscilan entre 201.27 €/MWh y 199.67 €/MWh. Estas franjas horarias constituyen una ventana amplia de precios bajos que los consumidores pueden aprovechar. En la jornada analizada se observa una **notable diferencia** entre la hora más cara y la más barata, alcanzando un pico de 260,62 €/MWh en la franja de 20:00 a 21:00, mientras que el precio más bajo se registra entre las 14:00 y las 15:00, con solo 26,25 €/MWh. Esta **amplitud de precios** resulta relevante para el consumidor, ya que indica que la elección del momento para consumir electricidad puede suponer un ahorro significativo en la factura final. A continuación, puedes consultar la tabla de precios horarios.
